reviews.title: Fast, best for the money 2TB PCIE4.0x4 game drive at the time I ordered it
reviews.comment: For gaming : Installation speed is limited by download speed or transfer speed from the drive your back ups are, and won't add to FPS. Gave it a 5 anyway since it's doing what I need it to do as a game drive - which is have reasonably fast PCIE4.0 and enough capacity (in this case, 2TB) for the least amount of money. In January 2024, this was the best value by my reckoning unless it underperformed in unexpected ways, or outright broke, but I can't test it longer term yet. So far it works as a game drive and photo editing drive. For media editing : Only re-did an HDR photo edit and it's really fast for that. DRAM cache would be a plus though if you're copying stuff into the drive but given the pricing for SSDs I decided to skip that for the ~3/4 game drive and ~1/4 temporary photo editing drive and instead of spending another $50 to $70 just for the DRAM cache I decided to just upgrade my DDR5 system RAM. If you edit media professionally you might want to still get DRAM cache. Ease of Install : This has to do with your laptop/motherboard+case than the NVME drive. It was easy on my 2023 TUF A15 (6800h, 3060), but YMMV on another computer. Value for Money : $95 for 2TB, PCIE4.0x4 was a great bargain in January 2024; but only because it isn't mid-2023 anymore when this and other drives were going for less. Added only as 3/4 game drive, 1/4 media editing drive (didn't actually partition it) but when I upgrade the included boot drive in my laptop when SSD health drops below 90% I'll probably get an NVME with DRAM cache depending on how prices are like by then.
reviews.author: Ezra99

reviews.title: Solid, Affordable High-Speed NVMe Drive That Delivers as Promised
reviews.comment: I purchased the Silicon Power 2TB US75 NVMe PCIe Gen4 M.2 2280 SSD to expand storage in a ProxMox server build, and I’ve been very satisfied with the results. The packaging was straightforward and easy to open, and although there were no detailed instructions included, anyone familiar with NVMe drives will find installation simple. It’s a standard-sized component, but the build feels solid and high-quality. Once installed, the drive performed exactly as advertised — offering excellent speeds and reliable performance. I specifically chose this model because of its impressive read/write speeds (up to 7,000/6,500 MB/s) and the very competitive price point. Compared to more expensive NVMe drives I’ve used, this Silicon Power drive holds its own, providing a cost-effective way to add 2TB of fast, responsive storage to my lab setup. The top strengths for me are definitely the price, capacity, and rated speed. These made it an easy choice for expanding my server’s storage affordably. The only minor drawback is that it does not come with a heatsink, which is important for installations in heat-sensitive environments like a PlayStation 5 or a high-demand server — so be sure to provide your own. Overall, I would absolutely recommend this SSD to anyone looking to expand storage on a PC, server, or PS5 without breaking the bank. I’d gladly buy this product again for future builds. ⭐ Rating: 5 out of 5 stars — For its price-to-performance ratio, capacity, and speed, this drive delivers excellent value and has worked perfectly in my setup. Tip for buyers: Make sure to add your own heatsink if using it in a system where cooling is critical.
